requirements.text: The FSW shall process science data from the camera and relay it to the Spacecraft Control Unit (SCU) in the form of CCSDS Source Packets.
The FSW shall receive commands from the SCU that establish the current instrument state and camera mode.
The FSW shall transmit detailed housekeeping data to the SCU in the form of CCSDS Source Packets.
The FSW shall receive a time message from the SCU and synchronize the XCP local copy of the spacecraft clock.
The FSW shall control the heaters on the telescope tube and on the thermal baffles.
The FSW shall read the TAM.
The FSW shall authenticate all incoming commands from the SCU using a cryptographic signature or sequence-based validation to ensure command integrity and authorization before execution.
The FSW shall ensure the integrity of transmitted housekeeping data packets using checksums or cyclic redundancy checks (CRC) to detect tampering or corruption during transit.
The FSW shall ensure that the Engineering Ethernet interface is physically or logically disabled in the Flight Unit (FU) configuration to prevent unauthorized access to the XCP.
The FSW shall process and packetize science data with a maximum end-to-end latency of <TBD> ms and maintain a throughput of at least <TBD> kbps without data loss.

The FSW shall maintain heater temperatures within <TBD> degrees of the setpoint and implement a fail-safe state to disable heaters if sensor readings exceed <TBD> degrees or indicate a hardware fault.
The FSW shall synchronize the local clock to within <TBD> ms of the spacecraft time and log a synchronization error if the 1PPS signal is lost for more than <TBD> seconds.
The FSW shall process and packetize science data such that the end-to-end latency from CCD readout to 1553 bus transmission does not exceed 50ms.
The FSW shall execute heater control loops at a minimum frequency of 1Hz with a temperature regulation precision of +/- 0.5 degrees Celsius.
The FSW shall be designed such that total CPU utilization does not exceed 70% during peak science data acquisition, with at least 20% of heap memory remaining available.
